text:
Sunil: Ran a full nsys capture against the midbatch hot path on the dedicated pool. Seeing a sharp latency bump tied to repeated cublasLt algo queries + workspace mallocs around 11:23:44. Perfetto + nsys attached below.
Kate: Can you paste the nsys command and the exact shape distro? Also which model and sequence lengths?
Sunil: Command was `nsys profile --output=midbatch --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=cpu cuda python -u serve_trace.py` — model is rtv2-medium, token lengths 16-64, batcher target 8-16, shapes mostly [1,4096,4096] after tokenization.
Ben: I think this is the kv-cache eviction interacting with batching. We saw logs like:
```
kv_cache: entry evict id=0x7f3a count=8 reason=slab_pressure
kv_cache: warmup miss id=0x7f3a hit=0
workspace: malloc 56MB at 11:23:44.123
```
Olga: Perfetto timeline shows a faucet pattern: matmul kernels launch in short bursts but cublasLt sometimes does an AlgoQuery path that triggers a workspace alloc+free between launches. That lines up with the eviction timing Ben posted. Kernel timeline: many short GEMM launches ~0.6-2ms, but intermittent 45ms stalls where workspace alloc dominates.
perf-bot: Automated summary: 11:23:44 - p99 latency 2.7x baseline, memory alloc churn increased 4.2x, cublasLt workspace allocations correlate with spikes.
Kate: Could be workspace fragmentation + small-batch algo flip. Two quick asks: 1) can you try preallocating a slab for CUDA workspace to avoid malloc/free? 2) try forcing a deterministic cublasLt algo for the most common shape and see effect.
Sunil: Will run A/B. Quick local test: forced ALGO=1 (env REDWOOD_CUBLASLT_FORCE_ALGO=1) for the 4096x4096 shape. Result: p99 dropped from ~320ms -> ~110ms on that path, but overall throughput dropped ~8% due to less optimal alos for some tail shapes.
Ben: If we do preallocated slab we can keep the dynamic algo probe but avoid alloc churn. We have a simple patch in runtime: prealloc_workspace(pool_id, size) + fall back. Also adding a cheap memo of last-good-algo per shape+seq_len helps (lightweight cache). Both should reduce probe frequency.
Olga: I posted a perfetto link: https://perfetto.local/trace/abc123 (internal) — look at the zoom at 11:23:40-11:24:00. You can see repeated cuBLASLtGetAlgorithm_v2 calls.
Kate: Nice find. Also let's check if kv_cache eviction threshold is too low for dedicated pool — maybe warmup policy evicts aggressively under short memory spikes. Can we bump eviction threshold or do sticky reservations for recent KV entries?
Sunil: Filed an issue: https://redwood.internal/issue/3421 - title: "mid-batch workspace alloc spikes + kv eviction -> p99". Assigning to eng-runtime and infra.
perf-bot: Suggested mitigation: enable workspace-slab (runtime flag) on canary, and set REDWOOD_CUBLASLT_FORCE_ALGO=1 for the problematic shape for 24h. Generated a canary rollout plan.
Ben: For immediate mitigation I pushed a short-lived fix on canary that preallocates 128MB slab per worker and enables kv warmup on batch boundaries. Observed reduced alloc churn in smoke run.
Sunil: Follow-up numbers from canary smoke: p50 unchanged, p95 down 18%, p99 down 62% for midbatch traces. Still seeing rare flips for small tail shapes.
Kate: Next steps: (1) land slab allocator + fallback memo (Ben), (2) tune kv eviction/warmup (infra), (3) run 6h soak with nsys captures at 1h intervals. Assign owners and add e2e reproducer.
Olga: I can add a perfetto rule to highlight cuBLASLtGetAlgorithm calls in future captures.
Sunil: Thanks all — I'll attach the full nsys .qdrep and perfetto links to issue #3421 and schedule a follow-up sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Kate: Great — please post exact commands you used for the A/B so SRE can replicate.
Sunil: Putting commands in issue (short):
```
# capture
nsys profile --output midbatch --trace=cuda,nvtx -w true --capture-range=timerange:1s:1m -- python -u serve_trace.py --load simulated
# force algo
export REDWOOD_CUBLASLT_FORCE_ALGO=1
# runtime flag
runtime --enable-workspace-slab --slab-size=134217728  # 128MB
```
Ben: Adding note: if forcing algo, validate generation quality & sampling because different algo can slightly change FP accumulation order -> tiny numeric diffs.
Olga: Also check quantized kernels if we flip algo; quant path has different workspace requirements.
Sunil: Will keep thread updated in issue. Thanks everyone. :wave:
